title: OC Nathaniel Hackett Press Conference | Week 9 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Gardner Minshew is the quarterback, and Hackett is tailoring the plan to him. Michael Wilson should keep his heavy route volume, and Hackett wants the run game to give the receivers a break.
summary: Hackett opened by warning that Seattle is very good. He said the offense runs on a large menu of concepts, and each week's plan is pulled from it based on the opponent and on what the quarterback, running backs, linemen and receivers do best. With Gardner Minshew in at quarterback, the staff is building a plan around what he is comfortable with while staying inside the same system. Hackett said Minshew did a fantastic job last week despite few reps with the first team. He added that Minshew has built chemistry with several receivers through scout-team work. He praised the backup quarterback in the room (named Carson, who is not on the roster provided) for his preparation, but said it may be a long time before he plays. He credited the clean pre-snap operation over the past month to constant emphasis from the staff and LaFleur, and he joked about the red zone struggles being behind them. He called Seattle's defense very well-versed and singled out a versatile defender who rushes, plays off the ball and covers receivers man-to-man. On workload, he said the two high-volume receivers are good enough that he wants them to keep running routes. He wants a steady run game to give them breaks and would prefer about 60 plays a game instead of the 80-play games they have had.

signals.claim: Minshew will run the offense against Seattle, with a game plan tailored to what he does well.
signals.note: The staff is designing the plan around Minshew's strengths, and Hackett praised his recent performance, so he looks like the starter for the Seattle game.
signals.quote: we're working with Gardner to make sure we do the things that he's successful at

signals.claim: Wilson will keep running a very high volume of routes and getting targets, with no planned workload reduction.
signals.note: Hackett dismissed overuse concerns despite Wilson ranking second in the league in routes run, so his volume should hold.
signals.quote: keep having them run routes over and over and getting them the ball

topics.detail: Hackett said he does not know how the backup quarterback, Carson (not on the provided roster), will handle the job until he plays, and that he may not play for a long time. He did not address the reported trade rumors directly. He said everyone is trained to be ready as a starter.
Minshew has worked more than anyone with Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (the names were garbled in the captions), mostly on the scout team. Hackett said that gives Minshew some comfort with them.

The offense draws each week's plan from a large menu of concepts. Hackett mentioned Trey McBride as a player who can do it all. He said the offense blocks the first level, the back beats the second, and the third level is where explosives come from. Over the course of a game, he wants the run game to take pressure off the receivers and would like about 60 plays instead of 80.

Penalties and pre-snap operation have been clean for a month because the staff and LaFleur have emphasized it. Hackett played down the earlier red zone struggles, saying it comes down to execution, and that the recent success came from continuing to work with the same menu of schemes.

Hackett called Seattle's defense very efficient and experienced, with every front and alignment. He praised a versatile defender (name unclear in captions) who rushes the passer, plays linebacker and covers receivers man-to-man. He also noted the crowd noise at Seattle.

title: Tommy Rees, Jeff Ulbrich, & Craig Aukerman speak in Madrid | Atlanta Falcons Press Conferences
headline: Rees takes the blame for the run-game slump (about 88.5 yards a game since Week 5) and says the offense needs to get back to explosive runs and red-zone rushing against a strong Bengals front.
summary: Rees called the Bengals' front seven their biggest strength. He praised Al Golden's defense for limiting explosive plays and said Dexter Lawrence is a game wrecker the plan has to account for. On the run game, he said the early-season explosive runs have dried up, teams now stack loaded boxes, and the fix starts with his play design and calls. He said run efficiency is still decent, but the offense must find ways to run into loaded boxes. He defended last week's rainy loss to Tampa as a matter of execution and play-calling, not weather. He said the staff kept throwing to try to hit one explosive play and adjusted as conditions changed. He called Michael Penix Jr. even-keeled and said the message to him is a week-to-week reset focused on decisions. On Drake London, he said they respect D.J. Turner's shadow coverage but can move Drake around to get favorable looks. He also acknowledged that red-zone rushing has dropped off lately (about 10 runs to 22 passes over four games) and said the best teams run the ball there. Finally, he said the offense's fix is a return to fundamentals and identity, with Bijan Robinson's blocking-based run game and isolating Drake as the keys.

signals.claim: The offense will work to restore its explosive run game and run more in the red zone, which should lead to more productive Bijan touches.
signals.note: Rees is publicly committing to fixing a run game that has fallen off since Week 5, which helps Bijan's outlook. The Bengals' strong front makes it a tough test, so it is not guaranteed.
signals.quote: when we block things the right way, what it looks like with Bijan

signals.claim: Drake will be moved around the formation to avoid D.J. Turner's shadow coverage and get better matchups.
signals.note: He may not be locked into one side or matchup, but facing top corners and bracket-style coverage is a recurring problem for his ceiling.
signals.quote: our ability to move Drake around and get him in different spots

signals.claim: Penix will reset from last week's rainy loss and focus on better decisions this week.
signals.note: Rees backed him as steady and blamed execution rather than the weather, with no hint of a lineup change.
signals.quote: Mike's pretty even keeled as you guys know him.

topics.detail: The team averaged about 181 rushing yards early but about 88.5 since Week 5. Rees says opponents have limited explosive runs and loaded the box, and he needs better designs and calls.
Over the last four games the team has had roughly 10 red-zone rushes against 22 passes. Rees said the best teams run it in the red zone and the offense must get back to doing so.
Rees said the staff kept passing at times to try to steal an explosive play and adjusted as the rain changed. He said the loss came down to execution and calls, not conditions.

Rees called the front seven their strength, with Dexter Lawrence a disruptive force and Al Golden's scheme built to limit explosives and let the front do the damage. D.J. Turner is a good corner who travels with the top receiver.
Rees praised Callahan's work ethic, fundamentals teaching, and command of protection, run, and screen games.

title: Coordinators Press Conference | Week 9 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: Idzik sees no decline in Bryce Young and says he'll lean more on play-action, keepers, screens and downfield shots to ease pressure after 11 sacks in two games.
summary: Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik was upbeat about practice after the bye and the short week. Most questions were about Bryce Young's recent dip in completion percentage and the 11 sacks he has taken in two games. Idzik said he doesn't see a decline in Young and took much of the blame himself. He wants to mix run, play-action, keepers and screens to keep defenses off balance, while still taking shots downfield. He praised Young for extending plays and for the 'second play mentality' he has shown. He also said Young needs to know his outlets and get to checkdowns faster, and that receivers must run routes with urgency even when they are late in the progression. Idzik denied that Young struggles against zone coverage and said the issue is making sure receivers and quarterback are on the same page about coverage. On the offensive line, he said a returning lineman who can play all five spots is creating competition, and that the best five will play Sunday, without naming starters. He also covered Detroit's trick play and how Denver's Alex Singleton triggers downhill, which calls for complementary run and pass concepts. Defensive coordinator Todd Wash then spoke about taking over the defense.

injuries.detail: A reporter said he is expected back in the next couple of weeks. Wash said he is out there moving around and deferred health updates to Dave Canales.
A reporter said he is expected back in the next couple of weeks. Wash said he is out there moving around and deferred health updates to Dave Canales.
Wash declined to give an update on his status and passed health questions to Canales.

signals.claim: The offense will use more run, play-action, keepers and screens, and keep taking downfield shots, to open windows for Young.
signals.note: A more varied play mix could ease pressure and bring back downfield production, but Young has been sacked 11 times in two games and his efficiency has dipped.
signals.quote: making sure that we're taking enough shots down the field

signals.claim: Young is being encouraged to extend plays and use his legs more.
signals.note: More scrambling and extended plays could add rushing and big-play upside, though Idzik said the rushing yards may not always show up.
signals.quote: a big piece that we want Bryce to tap into

topics.detail: Idzik said a returning lineman who has played all five spots is adding competition and communication to the room, along with a veteran who returned the previous week. He did not name a lineup and said the best five will play Sunday.
Idzik tied Young's recent struggles to a clean pocket up front, to receivers staying disciplined in their routes, and to getting the ball out urgently to checkdowns before the defense collapses.

Idzik said Denver's Alex Singleton triggers downhill when he gets a static look. Carolina plans complementary run and pass concepts so Denver cannot key on one presentation, and he asked skill players to report when a defender jumps a route early.
Asked about Detroit's CFL-style motion play, Idzik said Carolina studies other teams' ideas every week and will add things that fit its own personality.

Interim DC Todd Wash said the defense will stay a base 3-4 with a more aggressive, attacking front. He will call plays from the sideline. He said Derrick Brown needs to face fewer double teams and he praised Marco Wilson.

title: Dennis Allen, Press Taylor, Richard Hightower recap win over Seahawks, look ahead to Buccaneers | Press Conference
headline: Press Taylor is spreading touches by committee: Rome Odunze keeps earning targets, Cole Kmet's role can't be filled by one man, and left tackle is unsettled ahead of a tough Tampa run defense.
summary: Taylor credited the Monday night win over Seattle to heavy preparation, since the Seahawks' variety of fronts and pressures meant Caleb Williams had far more run-play kills and checks than usual. He said Williams handled the stress of that week well and looked in control on game day. He described the quarterback's improved completion rate as a product of decisiveness: the ball comes out on time, or he goes quickly to a checkdown to keep the offense on schedule. Taylor praised Rome Odunze's blocking and said the receiver has been rewarded with the ball in recent weeks, but he denied any forced feeding and said targets will stay by committee. D'Andre Swift was called reliable and trusted, with the staff managing his freshness, and he was a big part of the improved red zone scoring. Sam Roush is on track, but there are many mouths to feed and his role will shift week to week. Taylor said no single player can replace Cole Kmet, so the scheme may look different. At left tackle, Ozzy Trapilo has been rotated in and is being prepared to start if Theo Benedet's health issues keep him out. Taylor expects a huge challenge from Tampa Bay's physical, well-schemed run defense.

injuries.detail: Taylor was asked if Ozzy Trapilo is ready to start if Benedet can't play. He said 'we'll see where we're at' with the health issues.
Taylor spoke of replacing Kmet's role by committee in the past tense, which implies he is unavailable. The reason and timeline weren't given.
He returned from a recent absence and ran a full game plan Monday night.

signals.claim: Odunze will keep getting targets and big-play chances, within a spread-around passing game.
signals.note: His blocking has earned him opportunities and a recent uptick in production, but Taylor said it's not force-fed and will stay by committee.
signals.quote: you want to reward him with the ball

signals.claim: Williams will keep carrying heavy pre-snap responsibility and play decisively to keep the offense on schedule.
signals.note: Faster decisions and more efficient play raise the offense's floor and volume of plays.
signals.quote: very in control the way we wanted to play that game

signals.claim: Swift remains a trusted lead back, with his workload managed for freshness, and will keep a red zone role.
signals.note: He got the edge on runs and punched in scores in the red zone, which helps his touchdown outlook.
signals.quote: he's a guy we count on, we trust and he's produced for us

signals.claim: Roush's passing-game role will vary week to week and may stay modest, with blocking duties at times.
signals.note: He is crowded out of targets by many talented pass catchers, so he is not a reliable fantasy option yet.
signals.quote: Now we have a lot of mouths to feed, if you will.

signals.claim: No single player will replace Kmet, so his role will be split among several players and the scheme may change.
signals.note: His targets and blocking duties will be split across several players, so the other tight ends and receivers don't get a clear boost.
signals.quote: there's not one person that's going to fill that role

signals.claim: Trapilo is being built up to start at left tackle if Benedet can't play.
signals.note: Offensive line stability affects the run game and Williams' protection.

signals.claim: Benedet's availability this week is uncertain because of health issues, and left tackle has been rotated.
signals.note: His status determines the left tackle rotation, which matters for the Bears' run game against Tampa's front.

topics.detail: Taylor called the Bucs a huge challenge against the run: big inside, sound tacklers, and they rotate coverage and show heavy boxes. He said the offense will need to be on the same page on where runs go and who has the big hat.
The offense put heavy emphasis on finishing drives after leaving points on the table early in the season. Taylor said it can't settle for field goals and the plan changes week to week.
Taylor isn't frustrated by the lack of continuity at left tackle and sees rotation as a way to keep players fresh and adjust to matchups. Benedet got the full load last week because of the matchup.
The Swift-to-Williams play was dressing up the same ball handling with a different look. Seeing the quarterback lined up in an unusual spot causes defensive hesitation.

title: Travis Switzer Press Conference : November 5th, 2026
headline: Shedeur Sanders took first-team reps in practice and looks set to start this week for Cleveland, and Switzer was upbeat about his command and mobility.
summary: Switzer said Shedeur Sanders had a good first day with the ones. He praised his urgency, his command of the huddle and his willingness to let it rip while still checking down when needed. He said Sanders stayed engaged while taking few reps, through quarterback-room work and walk-through snaps. He called Sanders athletic enough to keep RPOs and designed runs in the plan, depending on the opponent and the defensive structure. On the run game, he pointed to the bigger picture from last week: turnovers, poor conversion downs, short-yardage and red zone failures, and falling behind into a drop-back game. He described protection problems as a mix of lost reps up front, backs getting beat and the ball not coming out quickly enough, not one single issue. The Saints defense will challenge Cleveland's run game and protection with interior linebackers and pressure, and the noisy indoor stadium puts a premium on communication, pre-snap penalties and the play clock. He said protections will operate as normal, with no sliding to help the new quarterback. He also said rookie tackle Spencer Fano was frustrated after the Steelers game but is capable of playing at his high standard.

injuries.detail: The injury report lists him as DNP with a toe issue, but Switzer did not address his health and only discussed how defenses are covering him.

signals.claim: Sanders takes over as the first-team quarterback this week and operates the full offense.
signals.note: He is stepping in as the starter, which raises the fantasy outlook for the Cleveland passing game, though Switzer never named him the starter outright.
signals.quote: I thought it was a pretty good day for him.

signals.claim: RPOs and designed quarterback runs can stay in the game plan with Sanders, depending on the opponent and defensive structure.
signals.note: Some designed-run or scramble upside is possible, though Switzer made it matchup-dependent.
signals.quote: he's still athletic enough

signals.claim: Defenses are starting to account for Boston differently in coverage, and he will keep adjusting to it.
signals.note: Extra coverage attention shows Boston is a productive target, but his toe injury (DNP) matters for his availability.
signals.quote: it means you've been productive

signals.note: The rookie tackle struggled against Pittsburgh and faces another strong pass rusher, which is a pass-protection risk for the new quarterback.
signals.quote: he's capable of that

topics.detail: Switzer blamed last week's loss on turnovers, poor conversion downs after lost-yardage and penalty plays, red zone failures and falling behind into a drop-back game. He singled out short-yardage and low red zone situations as the biggest disappointment and said the scheme there is under review.

He said protection problems were not one issue: linemen need to trust their technique, backs got beat once or twice, and the ball has to come out quicker. Communication was better than against the Jets.

Cleveland will use silent counts in the gun, as in every road game, and is focusing on getting in and out of the huddle quickly and shortening play calls. Protections will operate as normal with no sliding changes.
He sees similarities to Fangio's scheme and said the Saints' interior linebackers will challenge both the run and pass game. He also said their 99 is playing as well as ever.

title: Petzing on intelligence of roster
headline: Jameson Williams' speed and red-zone work are driving the offense (5 TDs in 3 weeks), Gibbs is praised as a complete back, and the run game plus 13 personnel are leaned on when it's working.
summary: Petzing spent most of the session on how the offense builds its creative looks. Ideas come from the whole staff, many get thrown out, and run game coordinator Hank leads the run-game formations. Mike Kafka pushed the CFL-style running-start play for weeks, and Petzing says he watches film from all levels of football. He stressed that the players' intelligence lets him add more to the game plan, though he sometimes trims it midweek if it gets too nuanced. He said the extra 13 personnel last week fit that game plan and was not a weekly emphasis, and he brushed off the poor early efficiency numbers for 12 and 13 personnel. He liked how the run game wore down the defense on the final drives and said it lets him lean on it late. He praised Jameson Williams for his speed, confidence and red-zone details, and said speed plus the run game puts defenses in a bind. He called Jahmyr Gibbs a complete back who takes pride in his blocking. He described the team as in a good place this week and the offensive line competition, with Juice Scruggs playing well, as a positive problem.

injuries.detail: Listed limited in practice with a rib issue. Petzing did not address it, and talked about using him on screens and motion.
Did not practice (ankle). A reporter asked about his status and Petzing did not give an update.
Listed limited with a chest issue. Not discussed in the press conference.

signals.claim: Williams will keep being used as a vertical speed threat and red-zone target.
signals.note: Five TDs in three weeks, and Petzing says his speed and confidence make him tough to defend, which supports a high-end WR role.
signals.quote: He's fast you know and I think he plays fast.

signals.note: Petzing praised Gibbs as a complete back, blocking included, which supports a full-time role.

signals.claim: St. Brown will keep getting the ball via screens, motion and different alignments.
signals.note: The staff is creating touches for him with momentum and screens, which is good for his floor, but his rib injury needs monitoring.
signals.quote: we threw him a couple screens against Arizona.

signals.claim: Scruggs and Cade Mays will compete for a starting O-line spot.
signals.note: If Mays' ankle keeps him out, Scruggs keeps the spot; the line's makeup affects the run game.
signals.quote: I don't look at it as a challenge. It's an opportunity.

topics.detail: The offset diamond and double-H-back looks came from staff ideas. Run game coordinator Hank leads this, and Kafka pushed the CFL-style running-start play.
The heavier use last week fit the game plan, not a new trend. Petzing says the team can run downhill from 11, 12 or 13 and downplayed the poor early efficiency numbers.
Petzing said the final two drives showed the run game working even when the defense knows it is coming. It also opens deep shots because defenses must choose between respecting speed and the run.
Petzing said the plan was for the second back to touch the ball, but his success and energy led to a carry or two more. The back isn't clearly identified, so no signal is attached.
Petzing said the team is right where it needs to be during an emotional week.

title: Eric Bieniemy: 'We Gotta Continue to Grow' | Press Conference 11/5
headline: Bieniemy says Kenneth Walker III needs more patience, but Emmett Johnson keeps his normal reps. Neither a backfield change nor any injury news was announced after the loss to Denver.
summary: Bieniemy opened by owning the tough loss to Denver and said the offense failed to execute when it mattered. He said Kenneth Walker III has played well overall but needs to let the game come to him and not press for the big play. He added that Walker has been working on this all year and that some games have gone better than others. Emmett Johnson will keep getting his normal reps. Bieniemy praised how he made the most of his chances, his work ethic, and his willingness to play special teams. He pushed back on the idea of a discipline problem, pointing to the penalties, turnovers and missed chances as lessons for a young offense at 5-2. He declined to blame one player for the fourth-and-one false start. On Xavier Worthy he praised the run blocking and effort but said he can improve. He also brushed past a question about Worthy running out of bounds. He called Cyrus Allen a young player who must play fast on every snap after a missed deep-ball chance. He briefly previewed the Jets, singling out linebacker Demario Davis, and said he doesn't worry about trade-deadline talk.

signals.claim: Walker remains the lead back but is being coached to run with more patience and take the available yards rather than hunt big plays.
signals.note: Bieniemy said Walker did not play his best and is still learning patience, which may mean fewer home-run attempts and a more steady, efficient approach.
signals.quote: allow the game to come to him.

signals.claim: Johnson will keep getting his usual share of offensive reps behind or alongside Walker.
signals.note: He has earned trust by making the most of his touches, so the committee split looks stable.
signals.quote: will continue getting his reps just like he normally does

signals.claim: Johnson is used on special teams (gunner, personal protector, kick return) and would likely return punts if asked.
signals.note: His willingness to take any role helps him stay on the field and earn trust, though it adds little to his offensive fantasy value directly.
signals.quote: There's no job that he will turn down.

signals.note: Bieniemy praised his run blocking and competitiveness but stressed he can improve and dodged a question about his recent alignment mistakes, so there is no clear sign of a bigger target role.
signals.quote: he's doing a great job of blocking in the run game.

signals.claim: Allen remains in the receiver mix but needs to play faster and finish plays, such as the deep ball he missed.
signals.note: He was singled out as a teaching point on a missed deep-shot chance, so his deep-target upside is unproven for now.
signals.quote: He's going to be okay.

topics.detail: Bieniemy rejected the idea of a discipline problem. He said the offense had chances to put away Denver and failed on 'game defining moments' through penalties and mistakes, and he expects the young unit to grow from it. The team is 5-2.

He declined to blame the player involved, referred to as 'Jalen' in the captions, saying it was not one player's fault. It is unclear whether that is WR Jalen Royals or OT Jaylon Moore, so no signal is attached.
Asked about the lack of completions of 20+ air yards, Bieniemy did not outline any scheme changes. He framed the issue as a young team learning to play every snap at full speed.
He said he is not distracted by deadline talk and will focus on preparing the players on the roster.

title: Mike McDaniel on Offensive Adjustments and Justin Herbert's Performance
headline: McDaniel plans to call plays from the box vs. Houston and is weighing an adjusted RB flow, with Omarion Hampton described as hungry for the ball, while the 0-7 offense keeps looking for answers.
summary: McDaniel said the offense is still not good enough after the Rams game. He praised the effort but pointed to too many reverts to old techniques and tightness, which reminded him of Week 1 against Arizona. The offense moved the ball in the first half but stalled in the red zone and isn't scoring enough. He said he gauges changes by how confident players are in what he asks them to do, and he is leaning on coach and player feedback. The biggest change is that he will try calling plays from the box this week, which he discussed with Harbaugh, and he is confident the staff can handle sideline communication. On the backfield, he said the starting RB is trusted, but the team has had strong conversations about adjusting the exact flow, and he's excited about someone dictating the rotation through play and prep. He defended Justin Herbert, saying he owned his responsibilities, that the interceptions had compounding variables, and that the game was a step in the right direction but not good enough. He took the blame himself for Herbert's struggles as a new coordinator. He also said he leans on concepts Herbert has had success with, and that this is the first week the starting lineup should be the same two weeks in a row. He expects Houston, under DeMeco Ryans, to be physical with elite edge rushers and to vary its coverages and pressures by opponent.

signals.claim: Hampton's share of the backfield work could change this week, with the rotation shaped by his play and preparation.
signals.note: McDaniel hinted at a possible change to the RB flow and said Hampton is eager for the ball, so his touches may rise, though McDaniel did not commit to a specific plan.
signals.quote: I can tell he's hungry for, for the ball and wants the opportunities.

signals.claim: Herbert will play better as the offense continues to fix its issues, though McDaniel said he is still short of what he is capable of.
signals.note: McDaniel saw progress against the Rams but admitted he hasn't gotten Herbert near his potential, so expectations should stay measured against a tough Texans defense.

signals.claim: The offense will lean more on pre-snap motion and on concepts Herbert has had success with, and McDaniel will call plays from the box.
signals.note: Scheme changes aimed at fewer turnovers and more consistent pass-game execution could help Herbert, but the results remain unproven.
signals.quote: I'm drawing upon a lot of things that Justin's had success with within our system

topics.detail: McDaniel plans to call plays from the box this week after discussing it with Harbaugh. He wants to see the whole field and relay adjustments to the position coaches between series. He said he is confident in the staff's sideline communication.

The offense moved the ball in the first half against the Rams but stalled in the red zone. McDaniel said the group reverted to old techniques, as in Week 1 against Arizona, and he takes responsibility. He said the team is coming closer together rather than splintering.
He praised coordinated blocking from the tight ends, tackles and interior line, and said the backs have been diligent in practice.

He discussed pure progression reads and defensive disguises, saying earlier-season issues with Herbert losing track of defenders were addressed through conversations. This week should be the first time the starting lineup is the same two weeks in a row.

McDaniel has known DeMeco Ryans for about 20 years. He expects a physical, hard-playing defense with elite edge rushers that is strong against the run and varies its coverage and pressure ratios by opponent.

title: Andrew Janocko on Mike Washington Jr.: 'Someone that continues to improve'
headline: Janocko praised the run-blocking progress, Cousins' short-yardage sneaks and Brock Bowers' role, but gave no concrete change to Jeanty's or Washington's workload.
summary: Janocko opened by crediting the scoring drive coming out of halftime against the Jets as a momentum swing the head coach had made a priority. He said the run blocking took a step forward, producing explosive plays and sustained drives. Asked about Ashton Jeanty's strong receiving production against his rushing struggles, he called running a team stat and said Jeanty is growing as a runner. He said rookie Mike Washington Jr. keeps improving in the passing game on fundamentals like hands and eyes. Kirk Cousins did most of the short-yardage work on sneaks because of what the staff saw on tape, though Janocko stressed that schemes change weekly. He said Cousins will throw to Brock Bowers even when Bowers is covered if Cousins feels he's open, and called Bowers a talent the offense uses in many ways. He was positive about Trey Zuhn's first career start at right guard after the line was shuffled. He said Tre Tucker was doing good things away from the ball even though he wasn't targeted much. The next game is at San Francisco, which he called a talented, experienced defense, now with DeForest Buckner added, and he noted a new play caller on the other side.

injuries.detail: Listed as limited with a concussion on this week's injury report. Janocko said nothing about his health and only praised his first start at right guard.

signals.note: The praise is about development in pass protection and routes, which could help his case for passing-down snaps, but no role change was announced.
signals.quote: he's somebody that continues to improve

signals.note: Janocko avoided criticizing Jeanty's rushing efficiency and pointed to receiving production, so his pass-catching floor looks stable while the rushing efficiency is still unresolved.
signals.quote: he's also been growing as a runner

signals.claim: Cousins may keep running quarterback sneaks in short yardage when the scheme and film favor it.
signals.note: Sneaks near the goal line can add rushing touchdown upside for Cousins and take carries from the running backs, but Janocko said the approach is matchup-dependent.
signals.quote: Things change week to week.

signals.claim: Bowers will keep being used in many ways and will keep getting targets even when covered.
signals.note: Cousins is told to trust Bowers even in coverage, which supports a high target share.
signals.quote: he's somebody that we try to utilize a bunch of different ways

signals.claim: Zuhn will continue to develop as the right guard after his first career start.
signals.note: A good first start at right guard suggests the offensive line shuffle is working and he could stay in the lineup, which helps the run game.
signals.quote: I thought Trey came out and competed well.

signals.claim: Tucker will remain a playmaker the offense tries to get the ball to, though his target volume has been inconsistent week to week.
signals.note: Janocko praised Tucker's work away from the ball but did not promise more targets, so his weekly production is still uncertain.
signals.quote: anytime his number's called, he's going to be ready to go.

topics.detail: Janocko said scoring at the end of the half and again coming out of it is a big statistical advantage. He credited the head coach for making it a weekly emphasis.
He said the run blocking against the Jets took a step forward, creating explosive plays and sustaining drives.

He described the 49ers as talented, experienced, well coached and opportunistic, with a new play caller and some new pieces. He said DeForest Buckner's return adds more talent to a defense that already knows each other.
Tyler Linderbaum gets everyone on the same page, and the assistant coaches got Zuhn ready for the right guard start.

title: Josh McDaniels 11/5: "The staff we have is tremendous across the board"
headline: McDaniels praises Drake Maye's October Player of the Month growth and DeMario Douglas's effort and blocking, and calls Green Bay's turnover-forcing zone defense a big challenge.
summary: McDaniels called Drake Maye's October Player of the Month award a team achievement. He credited Maye for fixing a lot of little things after a shaky September. He spent a lot of time praising WR coach Todd and the staff for individualized instruction in a receiver room that has seen heavy turnover. He called the Packers' defense well coached, with a physical front, instinctive safeties and nickel, and few big plays allowed, so offenses have to execute 8-12 play drives and avoid mistakes. He said DeMario Douglas stands out for energy, preparation, effort on every rep and blocking. He explained that Maye handles pressure through repetition, mastery of the protections and his work as a pocket passer. He said he wants the quarterback setting protections at the line so he can play faster with less doubt. Asked about missing top receivers and the run game, he said injuries hit every team, that running the ball keeps the offense balanced and out of long-yardage situations, and that the team has good backs. He did not name who is unavailable.

injuries.detail: Listed as a full practice participant (shoulder) on the injury report; McDaniels did not discuss it.
A reporter mentioned top receivers being unavailable. McDaniels said teams deal with 'one, two, three guys' missing but named no one and gave no status updates.

signals.note: Maye is trending up after being named October Player of the Month, and his coordinator credits improved details and pocket play.
signals.quote: improving as September finished and got into the next month of the season

signals.claim: Maye will keep setting protections and run the offense from the line of scrimmage.
signals.note: His command of protections is what McDaniels credits for his composure against pressure, which supports a stable QB floor.
signals.quote: I think it's repetition and I think it's confidence in the protections.

signals.note: McDaniels praised Douglas's habits, effort and blocking, which supports a continued role while the receiver room is thin.
signals.quote: the smallest guy we have, and he might be our best blocker

topics.detail: McDaniels called Green Bay a really well-coached, mostly zone unit with a physical front, instinctive safeties and nickel, and few big plays allowed. It capitalizes on mistakes, so the offense will need to sustain long drives.

McDaniels said running the ball keeps the offense balanced and out of long-yardage situations that lead to turnovers. He said the team has good backs who can also catch the ball, and that injuries are not unusual.
He praised the WR coach Todd for individualized preparation and instruction for each receiver, naming A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Kyle Williams among those in the room.

title: Doug Nussmeier on self-scout, run game | Saints vs. Browns 2026 NFL Week 9
headline: Nussmeier gave no concrete run-game fixes after the bye-week self-scout, and no timeline for rookie WR Jordyn Tyson's return, though he stressed Tyson will face a learning curve.
summary: Nussmeier spent most of the session explaining how the Saints self-scout. Analytics staff feed the coaches data all season, and the bye week allowed a deeper study. He said efficiency numbers can mislead, so coaches have to watch each play to learn whether it failed because of the scheme, the technique or the look the defense gave. Asked about the season-long run-game problems, he said the bye let them review every run play and direction, and that the fix could be a scheme change or better teaching of technique. He also noted that defenses adapt, which forces the offense to counterpunch. He did not name any specific schematic changes or personnel changes in the run game. On Jordyn Tyson, he praised his rehab and work ethic and called him an explosive playmaker. He cautioned that young players have a learning curve and that Tyson hasn't played much, and he gave no return date. He said Audric Estime, who has been away for 7-8 weeks, will need a short re-acclimation period but knows the system well, so the transition shouldn't be big. He also stressed a next-man-up mentality because of injuries.

injuries.detail: Rookie has been rehabbing and traveled to Paris with the team. Nussmeier said 'whenever we get Jordan back' and gave no timeline.
Has been gone 7-8 weeks and is coming back. Nussmeier expects a brief re-acclimation period and a quick transition.

signals.claim: Tyson will return to the field once cleared, but no date was given.
signals.note: The rookie WR is the key addition to monitor, but there is no firm return timeline, so don't count on him for Week 9.
signals.quote: we're looking forward to whenever we get Jordan back, getting him back on the field

signals.claim: Tyson's production may be limited at first because of the missed time and a rookie learning curve.
signals.note: Nussmeier praised his talent but openly tempered expectations, so his early fantasy output may be modest after he returns.
signals.quote: there's learning curves and I don't care how good you are coming out of college

signals.claim: Estime will return after 7-8 weeks away and be back up to speed quickly because he knows the system.
signals.note: His return adds depth to the backfield, but no role or snap expectations were described.
signals.quote: his transition is not going to be a big one

topics.detail: Analytics departments supply tendency data all season, and the bye week allows a deep dive. Coaches watch each play to separate truly good plays from ones that only worked because of circumstance, then look at what other teams do well.

The bye-week review covered every run play and direction, with the aim of identifying whether failures come from scheme, technique or the defensive look. No specific changes were announced, but he said defenses adapt, so the offense has to counterpunch.

Run-game planning is collaborative. Nussmeier works with Kellen Moore and the run-game coaches, and the plan then goes to the rest of the staff. He also stressed a next-man-up mentality because of injuries.

title: OC Matt Nagy on J.J. McCarthy's first start: 'The moment wasn't too big'
headline: Nagy says Malik Nabers remains the offense's focal point and J.J. McCarthy impressed in his first start, while the backfield is in flux without Tyrone Tracy Jr., with Devin Singletary praised and Cam Skattebo and Gregory Desrosiers in the mix.
summary: Nagy credited Malik Nabers' production to his playmaking, to complementary receivers who help him get open, and to the staff learning which routes he likes. He said the run game stays a priority even though the backfield is thin without Tyrone Tracy Jr., and that the backs will be put in spots that fit their strengths. Newer backs must learn the whole playbook, and Nagy said they have looked good mentally and physically over the last couple of days. He praised Devin Singletary's professionalism while he sat inactive and his touchdown against Houston. On J.J. McCarthy, Nagy described him as calm and stoic, said the moment wasn't too big for him, and said the offense is still being built around him. He expects the play-action, vertical-shot and QB-driven run elements to continue. He said Malachi Fields can give the team a lot more but that there is only one football and Nabers must get his catches. Nagy also showed respect for the opposing defensive coordinator Vic, expected some new looks, and said he is happy with the current roster ahead of the trade deadline.

injuries.detail: The question assumed the running back room is without him, and Nagy referred to him in the past tense ('weeks ago with Tracy'). No specific injury or timeline was given.

signals.claim: Nabers will keep getting a heavy target and catch volume as the offense's primary receiver.
signals.note: Nagy described getting Nabers a bunch of catches as a priority, which supports his high weekly floor.
signals.quote: we have this fiduciary responsibility to get Malik a bunch of catches

signals.claim: McCarthy remains the starting quarterback and the offense is being built around him.
signals.note: Nagy's praise of his composure in a first start suggests he keeps the job and the staff is committed to his development.
signals.quote: The moment wasn't too big.

signals.claim: The offense will keep using play-action, vertical downfield throws and QB-driven runs with McCarthy.
signals.note: His legs and the downfield passing are the stated strengths, which helps both his rushing and passing outlook and his receivers' deep-target upside.
signals.quote: the drop back game or play action game with some of the vertical downfield throws

signals.claim: Singletary will be part of the running back rotation now that Tracy is out.
signals.note: Nagy gave him strong praise and he scored against Houston, so he is a likely contributor, but no workload split was given.
signals.quote: He never became negative. He never made it about him.

signals.note: Nagy listed him among the backs to lock in on without committing to a lead role, so check his workload before using him.
A recent addition who could see snaps with Tracy out, though Nagy only said the new backs are getting reps and have done well in practice.
signals.quote: mentally, physically, they've done a good job

signals.claim: Fields will have a larger role in the passing game as he develops.
signals.note: Nagy sees a lot more room for him, but Nabers' target priority caps his volume and the rookie's time is still 'going to come'.
signals.quote: He can give us a lot more.

topics.detail: Nagy stressed keeping the run game going and not becoming one-dimensional, citing the Houston game. He said whoever carries the ball must be efficient.
Nagy praised defensive coordinator Vic, whom he worked with for a year, as adaptable, and expects some changes and unusual looks aimed at a young quarterback.
Nagy said he loves the current group and would give input if the front office added a weapon, but he did not push for a move.
The staff will cut plays McCarthy is not comfortable with by Friday and add ones he wants. Many concepts are still new to him, so the offense is still being built around him.

title: OC Frank Reich, S Minkah Fitzpatrick & LB Demario Davis Preview Jets-Chiefs | Press Pass
headline: Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol, so expect Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. to carry the WR load; Breece Hall is the 'bell cow' but Braelon Allen keeps a share.
summary: Frank Reich said the offense has turned the page and is focused on a tough Chiefs defense run by Steve Spagnuolo. He called the red zone a clear problem: the team reached it six times last week but scored touchdowns only twice, and he said the staff will both scheme it and coach it better. On the backfield, he called Breece Hall the 'bell cow' as he potentially returns, but said it will be a mix with Braelon Allen. He declined to commit to a hot-hand approach and called that an in-game feel decision. He praised the play-action game, crediting better protection and Geno Smith's patience and deep-ball skill, and said the offense has been efficient on intermediate throws. With Garrett Wilson in the concussion protocol, he said the team can't replace him but is confident in Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The offense would just look slightly different without him. He liked having vertical threats at several spots, said he prefers spreading the ball around even though some players will go quiet in a given game, and described Allen as an every-down back who is strong in protection.

injuries.detail: In the concussion protocol. Reich is planning for his absence while saying 'if Garrett's up' they'll run Garrett-style plays. The injury report lists him as limited.
The reporter framed him as potentially coming back. Reich treated him as the lead back and gave no health details.
Listed as limited with an ankle issue on the injury report. Reich did not address it.

signals.claim: The offense is preparing as if Wilson may be out and will shift its approach depending on whether he is cleared.
signals.note: His status is uncertain and is the key lineup variable for the Jets' passing game this week.
signals.quote: You can't replace Garrett Wilson. I mean, he's a unique player.

signals.claim: Mitchell will be a featured vertical receiver, especially if Wilson is out.
signals.note: Coming off a big game with a long post route, he is the likely beneficiary of Wilson's absence and offers deep-play upside.
signals.quote: I don't know what's better, the throw or the catch. I mean, they're both phenomenal.

signals.claim: Cooper will keep a role as a vertical receiver, though targets may be uneven in a given game.
signals.note: Reich praised his recent game, but he conceded some players get few touches in a given week, so Cooper's volume could swing.
signals.quote: you see the game Cooper had.

signals.claim: Hall will be the lead back on his return but will share work with Allen.
signals.note: Reich calls him the bell cow, but a split means his volume may not be fully workhorse.
signals.quote: Breece is obviously the Bellcow. He's our guy.

signals.claim: Allen will keep getting a meaningful share of carries alongside Hall rather than dropping out of the rotation.
signals.note: Reich praised his all-around game and protection but would not commit to a hot-hand approach, so his carry total is uncertain.
signals.quote: He can do everything.

signals.claim: The play-action game will keep generating efficient intermediate and deep throws, with Smith as the driver.
signals.note: Smith is playing well in play action, which supports his passing efficiency and the pass catchers' volume.
signals.quote: He's really good at the play action stuff.

topics.detail: The Jets reached the red zone six times last week but scored touchdowns on only two trips. Reich said there is urgency, and both the scheme and execution need to improve.
Protection has improved, and Reich praised the efficiency on intermediate throws plus the deep shots and check-downs to backs and tight ends. The goal is to hit all three levels.

Reich likes spreading the ball to many weapons because it forces defenses to fear more players, even though it's hard to get everyone touches in one game. He cited vertical threats in Mitchell, Wilson, Cooper and tight end Kenyon Sadiq.
Reich said the offense is making progress but needs more points and wins. He said the team is going 'one zero' each week.

opponent: Kansas City Chiefs (Week 9, at Arrowhead Stadium)

title: Brian Fleury Recaps Week 8 & Discusses Drew Lock Getting The Start vs. Cardinals
headline: Drew Lock starts vs. Arizona with Sam Darnold sidelined; Charbonnet and Price return to a week-to-week, ramp-up-based split.
summary: Fleury said Drew Lock is the starter against the Cardinals. He has already called plays for Lock in two games this season, including against this same opponent, so the game plan came together quickly and the staff is confident. He blamed Monday's loss to the Bears mainly on third-down execution against the league's best third-down defense, and said coaches and players all share responsibility. He was generally satisfied with an offensive line that had several new pieces and new communication, including Quenton Nelson, but said there is room to grow. He expects the line to come together sooner rather than later. Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are both back but at different stages of ramping up their conditioning. Their workload will change week to week through the bye, with certain game-plan plays earmarked for one or the other. He sensed Darnold was dealing with something unusual on Monday even though Darnold insisted he was fine. He said Grey Zabel was never at risk of being replaced by Anthony Bradford, and that the run game is close and just needs to be more focused.

injuries.detail: Did not practice (ribs) and Lock is starting. Fleury said he sensed Darnold was playing through something unusual on Monday.
Back from injury and still ramping up conditioning; his workload will be managed week to week.
Back from injury and still ramping up conditioning; his workload will be managed week to week.
Listed as limited in practice with an elbow issue. Fleury did not address it and is preparing for him to start.
Listed as DNP (knee) on the injury report. Fleury did not discuss his health, only how the run game used him on Monday.

signals.claim: Drew Lock will start at quarterback vs. the Cardinals and run the full offense.
signals.note: Lock steps in as the starter with a coordinator who is comfortable with his preferences and who has already called plays for him against Arizona this season.
signals.quote: he can handle everything they're going to throw at us

signals.claim: Darnold was playing through an undisclosed issue on Monday and is not the starter this week.
signals.note: Darnold's availability is uncertain, so Lock holds the QB value for now.
signals.quote: something going on that was a little bit out of the ordinary

signals.note: The backfield split is not settled, so his weekly volume is hard to project.
signals.quote: this week will be slightly different than next week

signals.note: Expect a fluid split rather than a clear lead back until after the bye.

signals.claim: Zabel remains the starting guard; Bradford was not considered for the start.
signals.note: Zabel keeps his role despite a rough debut at guard, so the line should stay stable in front of the QB and RBs.
signals.quote: We felt like gray gave us the best chance to win.

signals.claim: The run game will keep building around blocks Nelson is comfortable with, carried over from Indianapolis.
signals.note: His fit with the run scheme should improve as the line gains continuity.
signals.quote: allow him to execute blocks that he was comfortable with

topics.detail: Fleury called third-down execution the main reason for the loss and the top priority to fix. He said staying on the field is what lets them sustain drives.
The line had many new pieces on Monday, and Fleury was overall happy given the circumstances. He expects the unit to click sooner rather than later.

He thinks the run game is very close and said the direction is not a big change, just more focused. Continuity at running back and on the line is the main need. He explained that the point of attack on a run play is not always the side the run is aimed at.

title: Zac Robinson on Setting the Tempo in the Trenches | Press Conference
headline: After a 300+ rushing yard, zero-passing-yard game, Robinson says someone must step up in the pass game vs. CHI; Mayfield's thumb is improving and TE Bauer Sharp's role will expand.
summary: Robinson said the offense only realized it might finish with no completions around the third quarter. Efficient first- and second-down runs kept them on the ground, and the line, tight ends, receivers and backs all blocked physically. He praised the tight ends as blockers and said Bauer Sharp's role will keep growing because he is also a threat in the pass game. Cade Otton is a Swiss Army knife who lines up in line and in the backfield, and Payne Durham loves contact. He said the gap and power runs have been effective because the offense keeps earning run opportunities on early downs, and they remain part of the inventory. He admitted the passing game has to improve against Chicago, saying the offense needs 'somebody to step up' and must simply throw and catch, and that pass protection is the key. Baker Mayfield's thumb is getting better by the week and the staff expects him ready for whatever type of game it is. He credited the offensive line for cleaning up early-season penalties and negative runs, and for gaining rhythm as Cody Mauch and Tristan Wirfs got back together. He called Jeffery Simmons, now with the Bears, a disruptive player who must be accounted for on every snap, and he expects creative looks from Dennis Allen's defense on Sunday night.

injuries.detail: Thumb is getting better by the week; the staff anticipates him being ready for whatever type of game is called Sunday.

signals.claim: Sharp's offensive role, including in the pass game, will be expanded going forward.
signals.note: A growing role for a tight end who is a good blocker and a capable receiver could create streaming or deep-league TE value.
signals.quote: We'll continue to, you know, expand his role

signals.claim: Otton will keep being used all over the formation: in line, in the backfield like a fullback, and as a move blocker.
signals.note: His versatility and heavy blocking duties keep him on the field, but the run-heavy plan could limit his target volume.
signals.quote: Cade is Swiss Army knife. He can do everything.

signals.claim: Durham remains a key blocking tight end in the run-heavy 12 and 13 personnel packages.
signals.note: He is valued as a blocker, so he offers little fantasy value unless his receiving role grows.
signals.quote: he's got a small tattoo on his arm for a reason. He loves it.

signals.claim: Mayfield's thumb will be good enough for him to play Sunday night vs. Chicago, whatever the game plan.
signals.note: Mayfield is expected to play, but the pass game was almost nonexistent last week and the offense still leans on the run.
signals.quote: baker's thumb is, you know, getting better by the week

signals.claim: Johnson made plays in the first half of the Carolina game when the offense needed to pass.
signals.note: He is one of the few receivers Robinson named as a positive in the pass game, so he is a candidate to see targets if the offense has to throw.
signals.quote: saw Tez Johnson show up

topics.detail: Gap, power and counter runs have been effective, and Robinson said the offense is earning run opportunities through efficient early downs. He said these runs have always been in the inventory, and the game flow decides how many they get to.

Robinson said the offense must 'throw and catch' and needs someone to step up. Pass protection comes first, and he expects to use play action, quick game and dropbacks. The run success should open up pass looks.

Penalties and negative runs from early in the season have been cleaned up, and the run game came to life starting in the Dallas game. Having Cody Mauch and Tristan Wirfs back together has built rhythm, though Wirfs missed all of training camp.

Robinson called Jeffery Simmons a game-wrecking presence against both the run and the pass, and expects Dennis Allen to add new looks in his second week with him. He described the Bears' defense as violent and physical with a talented front, and expects a big Sunday night atmosphere.
